setup.title: FIRST-TIME SETUP
setup.lang_help: Pick the overlay language. Game data and official names (Deutsch, Español, Français, 简体中文) download once in a later step.
setup.gw2_help: Create an API key at ArenaNet's website. Copy the URL below and paste it in your browser:
setup.gw2_create: Create a 'New Key', name it anything, and select these permissions:
setup.enter_validate: Enter your key and click Validate
setup.ai_intro: Choose an AI provider and enter your API key. The optimizer uses AI for build synergy reasoning.
setup.ai_howto: The addon needs an API key from an AI company. You do not have to pay. Most people make a free OpenRouter or Google account and stay on free models.
setup.ai_pick: Pick OpenRouter or Google below. The URL opens a sign-in page - create a free account if you do not have one, then make a key and paste it here.
setup.gemini_howto: Google AI Studio - free Gemini models with a Google account:
setup.gemini_steps: The page asks you to sign in with Google (Create account if you need one). Then create an API key, pick any project, and copy it. The free tier is enough.
setup.openai_howto: OpenAI - this path usually needs a paid account. OpenRouter or Google are free:
setup.openai_steps: Sign in, click Create new secret key, name it, and copy the key. Billing has to be set up on the OpenAI account.
setup.anthropic_howto: Anthropic - this path usually needs a paid account. OpenRouter or Google are free:
setup.anthropic_steps: Sign in, click Create Key, name it, and copy the key. Billing has to be set up on the Anthropic account.
setup.openrouter_howto: OpenRouter - one key, many models, including free ones:
setup.openrouter_steps: The page asks you to sign in first (Google, GitHub, or email - Sign up if you need an account). Then create a key, name it, and copy it. Skip adding credits: free models work at $0. After setup, leave Free on in Settings.

explain.run_started: What you asked for: game mode, scale and role, then the goals that weigh most. A weight is how much one goal (power, condition, boons, healing, sustain, control) counts toward a build's score. Every build in this run is ranked by the same weights.
explain.data_skills: {profession} skills ({skills}): every entry the GW2 API tags with {profession} alone. {weapon} weapon, {utility} utility, {heal} heal, {elite} elite, {mechanic} profession-mechanic and {other} other skills (toolbelt, kit and bundle). Each attunement, stance and chain variant is its own API entry, so this is more than the buttons on your bar.
explain.data_traits: {profession} traits ({traits}): {specs} specializations x 12 (3 minor + 9 major), the traits the Hero panel shows. The data also holds {extra} elite weapon-proficiency traits that are granted automatically; they are not counted here.
explain.data_db: Whole database: {all} skill entries in the API dump. {prof} of them belong to a profession ({shared} are racial skills shared by several). The other {rest} are chain follow-ups, flip skills, kit and bundle skills, pet and creature skills and effect-only entries that never sit on a skill bar by themselves. {db_traits} traits = {db_specs} specializations x 12, plus {db_extra} elite weapon-proficiency traits.
explain.baseline: Your equipped build is scored by the same judge as every candidate, so a result that ranks below what you already wear is refused instead of offered.
explain.tier_beam: Tier 1 of 3. A beam search: it keeps the best {beam} complete builds and keeps changing one piece at a time (specs, traits, weapons, gear, runes, sigils, relic, skills), scoring every variant. It stops when {patience} generations in a row find nothing better, at {limit} s, or at {budget} evaluations.
explain.tier_deterministic: Tier 2 of 3, used only when tier 1 failed. It picks specializations, traits, rune, sigils, relic, weapons and skills one after another by how well they work together under your weights. No search, so it is quick and always answers.
explain.tier_legacy: Tier 3 of 3, the last resort when tiers 1 and 2 both failed: an older search over stat prefixes and specialization combinations.
explain.tier_choya: Choya composes the build in chat. The model proposes; the addon checks every pick against the game data and measures the result.
explain.fallback: The tier above stopped with an error or found no build that passed the checks (the reason is on its line). The run is not lost: the next tier is a simpler method that still ends in a build.
explain.seeding: The search starts from the build the synergy engine picks for your goals; every generation varies it from there.
explain.seed_repair: The starting build failed a survival check for this scenario (for example too little cleansing or stability). Each round swaps utilities, relic and sigils to fix it. 'evals' counts builds scored so far.
explain.seed_repair_receipt: Result of the repair above: which survival checks failed before and after. 'shortfall' is how far below the requirement the build still is (0 = passes).
explain.meta_seeds: Published builds from GuildJen, Hardstuck and Snow Crows for your profession and goal, used as extra starting points next to our own (at most 5). They must honour your locks and are scored like everything else; nothing is copied without being ranked.
explain.permuting: A generation is one round of the search: each of the {beam} builds kept so far has variants made from it (one piece changed), and every variant is scored. An eval is one full scoring of one build: stats, a rotation simulation and the survival checks. Limits: {budget} evals or {limit} s, and it stops early once {patience} generations in a row bring no better build.
explain.funnel: Search statistics. generated: variants made from the kept builds. admitted: variants that follow the game rules and your locks and were worth scoring. scored: evaluations spent. distinct_ranks: how many different scores came out (low means many variants tied). vs seed: how many variants scored better than (beat), the same as (tied) or worse than the starting build. The rest is diagnostics for bug reports.
explain.search_receipt: Search receipt: evaluations and generations actually used and the time taken, then the limits (budget, beam width, time limit, patience). improved_at_gens lists the generations that found a better build; the head values describe the winner.
explain.llm_advisor: The model suggests a few changes to the best build. Each suggestion is scored by the same judge and kept only if it ranks higher; the model never overrides the score.
explain.fine_tune: One pass tries a different stat prefix on each gear piece, one piece at a time, and keeps a swap only if the whole build ranks higher. Up to 4 passes, so up to 4 pieces can end up with different stats.
explain.det_pick: One step of the synergy engine: every option from the game data is scored against your goals and the best one is kept.
explain.measuring: Plays the build's rotation for {secs} s against a training dummy set up for this scenario (not a real fight) to get damage, boons and healing. Synced community builds are measured the same way for the % comparison.
explain.kept_baseline: No tier found a build that ranks above your current one under these goals, so your build is kept rather than offering a worse one.
explain.enrich: The model writes the explanation text for the top result. It does not choose the build.
explain.llm_request: Request {n} of this run to {provider}, model {model}.
explain.llm_tokens: in = prompt tokens: everything sent to the model (instructions, game data, your build, the chat so far). out = completion tokens: what the model wrote back. A token is a piece of text, roughly 4 characters. Providers bill per token, and the cost in the run header is computed from these counts.
explain.wait_quota: The {provider} free tier allows only a few requests per minute (Gemini: 5 per model). The run waits for the next free slot instead of failing. This time counts as LLM wait in the run header, not compute.
explain.wait_retry: {provider} answered busy or with a temporary error. The same request is sent again after this pause. This time counts as LLM wait in the run header.
explain.record: Saved to {path}, one line per run. The Generations tab reads it. Nothing is sent anywhere.
explain.choya_handshake: A short check of how this model behaves: whether it can call tools (native, sloppy, none), how cleanly it returns JSON (strict, wrapped, prose), how long the probe took, and its record here (runs, repairs, failures, seconds per round). Remembered per model, so the probe is only sent when needed.
explain.choya_reference: The optimizer's own build for this scenario, worked out without the model. Choya is shown it as an answer to match or beat; the line shows how it scored.
explain.choya_prompt: The context sent with your message: mode, scale and role, your character's current build and gear, the build on the results tab, pasted chat codes, the last few chat messages and the reference build. The number counts characters of that context only (the fixed instructions are sent too); roughly 4 characters make one token.
explain.choya_attempt: Choya composes a build. At most 2 attempts: if the first is refused, the second is told exactly which check failed.
explain.choya_lookup: The model asked the addon to look things up in the game data (the tools named on the line). Each round is one more request to the model; at most {max} rounds.
explain.choya_repair: The reply described a build in words instead of the structured form, so the addon read the build out of the text.
explain.choya_validating: Every name in the reply (specializations, traits, skills, weapons, gear, runes, sigils) is checked against the GW2 API data. Picks that do not exist or are not allowed for this profession are fixed or refused.
explain.choya_no_plate: The reply was conversation without a complete build, so there is nothing to check or measure.
explain.choya_accepted: The build passed the checks and ranks well enough against your current gear and the reference build.
explain.choya_refused: The build failed a check (the reason is on the line). Your gear is not changed; Choya gets another attempt if one is left.
explain.choya_plating: Turning the accepted answer into a build card with stats, gear and skills.
explain.choya_fallback: The model did not answer (timeout, quota or error), so a fallback reply is shown instead.
gen.tip_explain_time: LLM wait: time spent waiting on the model, including quota pauses and retries. Compute: everything the addon did itself (search, simulation, checks).
gen.tip_explain_tokens: Tokens are pieces of text, roughly 4 characters each. Prompt = sent to the model; completion = written by it.
gen.tip_explain_cost: The cost is an estimate: tokens times the price in the bundled price table (row and date above), or the cost the provider reported. Free tiers cost nothing.
gen.tip_cost_partial: Cost n/a: the provider reported a cost for only some requests
gen.thread_failed: Could not start the worker thread - the system refused it. Try again.
gen.empty: No generations yet. Every New Build, Improve and Choya run is recorded here.
gen.open_hint: Open this build on {character} in {scenario}. Switching character clears the results strip.
gen.open_busy: Wait for the current run to finish.
